source.title: Normalized Direction-preserving Adam
source.authors: Zijun Zhang; Lin Ma; Zong-Peng Li; Chuan Wu

record.tranche_reason: Compares test error for Adam, SGD and an Adam variant on image classifiers; this conceptually tests the optimizer and generalization part of V4 with a different benchmark and training setup.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior findings about memorizing natural and noise data, but does not test them. Its own optimizer comparisons report test error. It does not report training error, so equal or better training performance cannot be assessed.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares vanilla Adam with momentum SGD on held-out CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 performance using WRNs and a cosine learning-rate schedule. Adam has higher test error in every matched comparison. This is an optimizer-generalization test, although SGD weight decay is also tuned and training performance is not reported.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct: the authors conclude that ND-Adam combined with regularized softmax substantially improves on vanilla Adam and eliminates the generalization gap to SGD in their image-classification experiments. This is their overall characterization, not exact equality in every table cell.
record.recipe_differences: Uses WRN-22-7.5 and WRN-28-10 on CIFAR-10/100, cosine learning-rate schedules, and Adam/ND-Adam comparisons; not a direct reproduction of the cited optimizer comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies with dataset, scaling-factor and softmax setup, and WRN implementation/size. Regularized softmax improves the reported test errors, especially for Adam.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed ND-Adam method improves over vanilla Adam; with softmax regularization it approaches or slightly improves on SGD in the reported comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Direction-preserving vectorwise adaptation and spherical weight normalization, combined with softmax regularization, can recover SGD-like CIFAR test performance.

record.problems: Only CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 image-classification experiments are reported. Table 1 and Table 2 give averages of 3 runs but no uncertainty estimates. Training performance is not reported, and the tested models are WRNs rather than the broader range of benchmarks in V4.

untested.parts: No natural-label versus random-label fitting experiment.
No width sweep beyond the width required for interpolation.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

No language benchmarks, broad hyperparameter search, Adam-to-SGD switching, or controlled decoupled-weight-decay comparison. Training performance is not reported, so the training-performance clause cannot be assessed. The tuning protocol also includes SGD weight decay, rather than exclusively learning rates and schedules.
No dropout comparison; dropout is not used.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or ranking of generalization-gap measures.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text interleaves the two tables, causing several extracted values to be assigned to the wrong settings. Corrected Table 1 BN-Softmax errors are SGD/Adam/ND-Adam: 4.49/5.43/4.14% on CIFAR-10 and 20.18/22.48/19.90% on CIFAR-100. Table 2 WRN-22-7.5 errors are SGD/ND-Adam: 3.84/3.70% and 19.24/19.30%. Results average three runs without uncertainty estimates. Proposed-method benchmarks are excluded under the requested own-method comparison rule; they do not receive a V4 verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Natural-label and random-label fitting and held-out accuracy are not tested.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No language benchmarks or broad hyperparameter tuning; training performance is not reported. The paper tests Adam and its ND-Adam variant against SGD on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.
No dropout comparison; the experiments state that no dropout is used.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measure or comparison of generalization-gap measures.

relationships.condition: Vanilla Adam versus momentum SGD, TensorFlow WRN-22-7.5 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, with trainable BN scaling factors
relationships.reason: R2 and R8 report Adam errors of 6.14% and 25.51%, versus SGD's 4.61% and 20.60% in R1 and R7.
relationships.display_finding: Reported test errors were higher for Adam on both datasets, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Vanilla Adam versus momentum SGD, TensorFlow WRN-22-7.5 with BN scaling factors removed and BN-Softmax
relationships.reason: R5 and R11 report Adam errors of 5.43% and 22.48%, versus corrected SGD errors of 4.49% and 20.18% in R4 and R10.
relationships.display_finding: Reported test errors remained higher for Adam after the normalization changes, but these comparisons remain unverified.
